la:verb:protrudo.html:
prō-trūdo, si, sum, 3, v. a.,
to thrust or push forwards, to thrust forth, push out (class.; syn.: proturbo, propello).
Lit.: moles protruditur,; and 280: cylindrum,: is . . . domo atque nostrā familiā protruditur, Afran. ap. Don. (Com. Rel. p. 174 Rib.; cf. Lachm. ad ); so, protrudi penatibus,to be thrust out of doors,.—
Trop., of time, to put off, defer: comitia in Januarium mensem,.

la:verb:protraho.gloss: to drag, pull, draw or bring forth or out (to a place)
senses: to drag, pull, draw or bring forth or out (to a place)
to bring to light, discover, disclose, reveal, expose
to lengthen out something as to time; prolong, protract, defer
la:verb:protraho.html:
prō-trăho, xi, ctum, 3 (sync. form protraxtis for protraxistis, .—
Inf. protraxe for protraxisse, ), v. a., to draw or drag forth, to bring forth or out, pull out, to draw to a place (class.; cf.: promo, profero).
Lit., : aliquem e tentorio,: me istam capillo protracturum in viam,: aliquem hinc in convivium,: Calchanta in medios,: aliquem in medium manibus suis,: ad operas mercenarias statim protrahi,: pedibusque informe cadaver (Caci) Protrahitur,: multa siti protracta corpora,: e tentorio,.—
Trop.
In gen., to drag forth, to draw or bring anywhere: aliquid in lucem,: ad gestum pueros,: quidquid paulatim protrahit aetas In medium, dub. (v. Lachm. II. p. 346): indicem ad indicium,: nudi in medium protrahebantur,. —
In partic.
To bring to light, discover, disclose, reveal, expose, betray: auctorem nefandi facinoris,: inimicum,: facinus per indicium,: publicanorum fraudes,: nec meus indicio latitantes versus amicus Protraheret,.—
To lengthen out any thing as to time, to prolong, protract, defer (post-Aug.; syn.: produco, propago): protrahere ac differre stipendia militum,: convivia in primam lucem,; cf.: epulas a medio die ad mediam noctem,: in serum dimicatione protractā,: sermones,.—Pass. in mid. force: quid diutius protrahor? why dwell longer on this? .—Absol.: quinque horas protraxit,i. e. he lingered for five hours,—
To weary, detain too long: ne diutius te protraham,.—
To extend, increase (post-class.): utrum hoc usque ad Graecum sermonem tantum protrahimus, an verum et ad alium ... dubitari potest,: insolentiam, (al. pertraheret).—
To bring or reduce to: ad paupertatem protractus,.

la:adv:protinus.html:
prō-tĭnus (less properly prō-tĕnus), adv.
tenus
,
before one's self, forward, farther on, onward.
Lit. (rare but class.; syn.: statim, continuo, actutum): praecepisse, ut pergeret protinus, quid retro atque a tergo fieret, ne laboraret,: ipse capellas Protinus aeger ago,

drive along before me, : quā (voce) protinus omne Contremuit nemus,far and wide,.—

Transf.
Right on, continuously, constantly, uninterruptedly (rare; not in Cic.).
In space, : trans Lygios Gothones regnantur . . . protinus deinde ab Oceano Rugii et Lemovii,: summa (vertebra) protinus caput sustinet,.—
In time or order: post ad oppidum hoc vetus continuo mecum exercitum protinus obducam,; Sisenn. ap. ; Tubero,: protinus ut moneam,: trajecto missa lacerto Protinus hasta fugit servatque cruenta tenorem,; : felix si protinus illum Aequasset nocti ludum,.—
Forthwith, immediately, directly, from the very first, instantly, on the spot (class.; but rare in prose until post-Aug. per.): oratio protinus perficiens auditorem benevolum,at the very outset,: hostes protinus ex eo loco ad flumen contenderunt,: tu protinus unde Divitias aerisque ruam, dic, augur, acervos,.—With a negative: non protinus,not immediately,.—With ex or ab, immediately or directly after: ex fugā protinus auxilia discesserunt,: protinus ab ipsā curatione,: a partu,: ab adoptione,; cf.: protinus post cibum,.—With ut, quam, atque, as soon as, as soon as ever; with ut: protinus ut percussus est aliquis,; ; .—With quam, (al. quā); 15, 17, 18, § 67.—With atque, —Prov.: Protinus ad censum, de moribus ultima flet quaestio,.

la:verb:protendo.html:
prō-tendo, di, sum and tum, 3, v. a.,
to stretch forth or out, to extend (not in Cic.; syn. porrigo).
Lit.: hastas, Wagn.: bracchia in mare,: supinas manus ad genua alicujus,: aciem (oculorum) in aestus pelagi,: cervicem fortiter,: cochleae bina ceu cornua protendentes contrahentesque,: protentis hastis,: pedes temo protentus in octo,: consanguineam protendere dextram,: praerupta protendit juga Cithaeron,.—Mid., to stretch forth or out, to extend: inter digitos medius longissime protenditur,projects,: protenditur ad Bactros usque gens Mardorum,reaches, extends,: anus haec in pellis periculum protenditur, is swelled out, distended with drink, Plaut. Fragm. ap. Schol. .—Of a river: usque ad colla cornipedum protentus,swollen,.—
Trop., to make long, to prolong, lengthen, extend (post-class.): utramvis partem in plura verba protendere, Oud.: praepositiones producere atque protendere,to prolong in pronunciation,; : barbare protendere,.—Hence, prōtentus, a, um, P. a., stretched out, lengthened, extended (post-class.): Phocis lucis in exortum protentior,extending farther,: protentior vita,.
la:verb:protendo.inflection: di, sum and tum, 3, v. a.

la:verb:proturbo.gloss: to drive, on, forward or away
senses: to drive, on, forward or away
la:verb:proturbo.html:
prō-turbo, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.,
to drive on or forward, to drive forth or away, to repel, repulse (mostly post-Aug.; not in Cic.).
Lit.: his facile pulsis ac proturbatis,: hostes telis,: apes pigras et ignavas,: extra tecta proturbantur,: aliquem de domo,: aliquem laribus,; : hostem Missilibus,: hostes hinc comminus,: in exsilium proturbatus,.— Poet.: silvas,to bear down, overthrow, prostrate,.—
Transf.: anhelatum murmur pectore,to send forth, utter,: militum conviciis proturbatus,attacked, assailed,: nuncius hunc (Aeolum) solio Boreas proturbat ab alto,drives him from his lofty seat,.

la:verb:protego.html:
prō-tĕgo, xi, ctum, 3, v. a.,
to cover before or in front, to cover over, cover, protect (class.; syn.: defendo, tutor).
Lit.: tabernacula protecta hederā,: rates cratibus ac pluteis,fin.: aedes,to furnish with a projecting roof,: hunc scutis protegunt hostes,to cover, protect,: se umbone,: caput contra solem,: scutis protecti corpora longis,: protegendi corporis memor,.—
In partic., to put up a shed, penthouse, or projecting roof (jurid. Lat.): hic in suo protexit,: jus proiciendi protegendive,.—
Trop.
To cover or shield from danger, to defend, protect (rare and class.): jacentem et spoliatum defendo et protego,: ad protegendum regem,: viros optimos,; : aliquem adversus criminantes,: causam,: Dominus exercituum proteget eos,. —
Transf., to ward off, keep off: hiemes,.—
To cover up, screen, conceal (very rare): nequitiam supercilio truci,: risu protectis insidiis,: parricidii immunitatem metu majore,.

la:verb:proterreo.gloss: to frighten, drive or scare off or away, terrify
senses: to frighten, drive or scare off or away, terrify
la:verb:proterreo.html:
prō-terrĕo, ŭi, ĭtum, 2,
to frighten or scare away, to drive away by terror, to affright, terrify (rare but class.): filium Proterruisti hinc,: aliquem adverso equo,: aliquem jaculo parmāque,: feras ardentibus facibus,; : patriā pulsus atque proterritus,: tu a tuis aedibus vi atque armis proterritus,; ; : proterritis hostibus atque in fugam conjectis,.

la:verb:protero.gloss: to trample down, tread on something
senses: to trample down, tread on something
la:verb:protero.html:
prō-tĕro, trīvi, trītum, 3, v. a. *
To drive forth, drive away: ver proterit aestas Interitura,i. e. supplants,.—
To tread under foot, trample down, wear away, crush, bruise (class.; syn. proculco).
Lit.: aliquem pedibus,: homines elephantis proterendos substravit,: januam limā,i. e. to destroy,: equitatus aversos proterere incipit,: agmina curru,: florentia arva,: adversum rota proterit agmen,: ulmus labens proterit uvas,: seges torrefacta proteritur,.—
Transf., in gen., to overthrow, beat, crush, defeat, destroy: Marte Poenos,: protrita hostium acies,: aliquem proterere et conculcare,to maltreat, abuse, trample upon,; cf.: pati urbem proteri atque conculcari,: ruinā suā proteri,: umbram,: omnia ferro,: barbaram plebem,. —Hence, prōtrītus, a, um, P.a., worn out (by rubbing); hence, of words, of frequent use, common, trite, vulgar (post-class.): verba,; ; .

la:noun:protervitas.html:
prŏtervĭtas, ātis, f.
id.
,
pertness, sauciness, boldness, impudence (class.): protervitas levior est quaedam contumelia, procacitas major, petulantia maxima, Don. : coërcere protervitatem, Pac. ap. (protervitates, acc. to Fest. s. v. redhostire, p. 270 Müll.); ; : urit me Glycerae nitor, Urit grata protervitas,forwardness, wantonness,.

la:noun:protectio.html:
prōtectĭo, ōnis, f.
protego
,
a covering over; trop., a protecting, protection (postclass.): fidei,: armorum,: Dei,.

la:adj:protervus.html:
prŏtervus, a, um, adj.
protero; qs. trampling on every thing; hence
,
violent, vehement.
Lit. (poet.): venti,: Africus,: Eurus,: stella canis,scorching, oppressive,.—
Trop., forward, bold, pert, wanton, shameless, impudent (class.; generally milder than procax and petulans; v. protervitas): petulans protervo animo sum, : homo,; : dictum aut factum,: vidua,: Satyri, turba proterva,: juvenes,: rixae,: frons,: oculi,: manus,: Musa,: lingua,: sal protervum,ribald wit,.—Comp.: meretrix protervior,.—Hence, adv., in two forms, proterve and proterviter.
prŏtervē.
In a bad sense, boldly, wantonly, shamelessly, impudently (class.): aedes arietare,: proterve iracundus, (immoderate, superbe, Don.): consectans aliquem proterve,.—Comp., .—Sup., , 5, 22.—
In a good sense, boldly, with spirit: confidenter pro se et proterve loqui,.—
prŏtervĭter, boldly, wantonly, shamelessly, impudently, Enn. ap. (Com. v. 8 Vahl.).
